title: Certification vs accreditation vs licensing: what is the difference?
description: Certification attests a person or system meets requirements; accreditation attests the certifier is competent; licensing is legal permission to work.
shortAnswer: Certification is an independent attestation that a person, product, process or management system meets specified requirements. Accreditation is a formal recognition that the body doing the certifying, testing or training is itself competent to do so. Licensing is permission granted under law, usually by a government regulator, to carry out an activity that is otherwise prohibited. A crane operator, for example, may need a government license or a certification from an accredited testing organization, and an employer evaluation on top.
keyTakeaways: Certification answers "does this person or system meet the standard?"; accreditation answers "is the certifier competent?"; licensing answers "is this person legally allowed to do the work?"
Certification of persons is governed internationally by ISO/IEC 17024, whose third edition was published in March 2026.
Licensing is usually mandatory and enforced by a regulator; certification and accreditation are often voluntary unless a law or contract requires them.
None of the three replaces workplace competence checks: OSHA's crane rule, for instance, says a certificate cannot by itself make an operator qualified.
Training records should state which of the three each credential represents, who issued it, its scope and its expiry.

sections.heading: What is the difference between certification, accreditation and licensing?

blocks.text: The difference is who is being checked and on what authority. Certification checks the person or system against requirements. Accreditation checks the certifier, tester or provider. Licensing grants legal permission, backed by an offense for working without it.

The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) [describes conformity assessment](https://www.nist.gov/standardsgov/conformity-assessment-basics) as including activities such as testing, inspection, certification, management system assessment and registration, "the accreditation of the competence of those activities", and recognition of accreditation programs. It notes that conformity assessment can be done by a first party (the supplier), a second party (the purchaser), a third party independent of both, or the government, which has a unique role where regulatory requirements apply. Terminology is set out in ISO/IEC 17000.

Licensing sits on the government side of that picture. Under the model Work Health and Safety Regulations used in most Australian jurisdictions, for example, a person must hold a [high risk work license](/regulations/high-risk-work-licence-requirements) to carry out any of the 29 classes of high risk work in Schedule 3, and the license expires after five years.

sections.heading: How do they compare side by side?

blocks.text: They differ in subject, issuer, legal force and what they prove. The table is a category level comparison with examples.

sections.heading: How do the three fit together in one role?

blocks.text: In many safety critical roles the three layers stack, and the employer still adds its own check. OSHA's rule for crane operators in construction, [29 CFR 1926.1427](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1926.1427), shows the layers clearly.

items: **Licensing or certification:** before operating covered equipment, the operator must be licensed where a state or local license applies, or certified by an accredited crane operator testing organization, or qualified through an audited employer program. Certification is valid for five years, and a license may be valid for no longer than five years.
**Accreditation:** the testing organization must be accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency, and its accreditation is reviewed at least every three years.

**Employer evaluation:** the employer must evaluate the operator's skills and ability to recognize and avert risk on the equipment, and document it. The rule states that a certificate cannot by itself make a person qualified.
**Training records:** the employer keeps the evaluation documentation alongside the license or certificate details.

blocks.text: The lesson generalizes. A license or certificate is an input to a competence decision, not the decision itself. That is the role of [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency); setting it up is covered in [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency). Detail on the crane rule is on [OSHA crane operator certification](/regulations/osha-crane-operator-certification-requirements).

sections.heading: How do these terms apply to training providers and programs?

blocks.text: For training, the same three ideas apply to providers and courses: a provider may be registered or licensed to deliver regulated qualifications, a course may be accredited, and a learner may be certified on completion. The labels vary by country, so read each scheme's own definitions.

items: **Registration of providers:** in Australia, registered training organizations operate under the [2025 Standards for RTOs](/regulations/standards-for-rtos-2025-training-and-assessment), which require trainers and assessors to hold credentials set in a Credential Policy.
**Sponsor approval:** US accountancy CPE sponsors can register with NASBA's National Registry of CPE Sponsors and must follow the AICPA and NASBA Statement on Standards for CPE Programs.

**Certification schemes for persons:** ISO says [ISO/IEC 17024](https://www.iso.org/standard/17024) can be used for accreditation, peer assessment or designation by governmental authorities, and that its 2026 revision addresses AI based assessment tools.

**Management system certification:** ISO notes that certification to its management system standards is optional and that [ISO does not perform certification](https://www.iso.org/iso-13485-medical-devices.html); independent bodies do.

sections.heading: Which do you need to check for a given role?

blocks.text: Start with the law, then contracts, then internal competence. Check whether a license is legally required, whether a certification is required by law, contract or customer, and whether the certifier's accreditation matters for acceptance.

items: Identify any license the law requires for the work and the regulator that issues it.
Identify certifications required by regulation, contract or customer, and whether they must come from an accredited body.
Record for each credential: type, issuer, scope or class, issue date, expiry and verification method.
Define the employer's own competence check for the specific equipment, site and procedures.
Set reminders for renewals and track any conditions on the credential.

blocks.text: A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) that lists credentials per role, with expiry dates, makes gaps visible before they become violations.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records licenses, certifications and accreditations as distinct evidence types linked to the role requirements they satisfy, with the issuing body and source rule. The employer's own competence assessment points sit alongside them, so an auditor can see both the external credential and the internal verification.

faqs.q: Is a certificate of completion the same as certification?
faqs.a: No. A certificate of completion shows that someone finished a course. Certification, in the conformity assessment sense, is an independent attestation that a person meets defined competence requirements within a scheme, usually involving assessment and periodic recertification under rules such as ISO/IEC 17024.

faqs.q: Can a person work with a certification but no license?
faqs.a: Only where the law does not require a license. Where a license is mandatory, as for classes of high risk work under the model WHS Regulations, certification or training alone is not enough. Where a rule offers alternatives, as OSHA's crane rule does, any one of the listed routes may satisfy it.

faqs.q: Does accreditation make a certificate valid everywhere?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Accreditation supports recognition and mutual acceptance, which ISO describes as a benefit of ISO/IEC 17024, but each regulator or customer decides which credentials it accepts. Some credentials, such as an audited employer crane certification, are expressly not portable.

Accreditation bodies, which are usually national and assess certifiers against international standards. NIST lists accreditation of the competence of conformity assessment activities as part of conformity assessment. Check whether the regulator or customer requires accreditation by a particular body.
